---
title: Using Plotly
---

By using `echo: false` the code will not show but the figure will. 


::: {.panel-tabset}

## Style 1

Example and solutions could go here. 



```{python}
#| echo: false

import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Define the function f(y) from the autonomous equation dy/dx = f(y)
def f(y):
    return y**2 - 4

# Create a range of y values
y_values = np.linspace(-4, 4, 100)
f_y_values = f(y_values)

# Create a pandas DataFrame for Plotly Express
df = pd.DataFrame({'y': y_values, 'f(y)': f_y_values})

# Create a line plot
fig = px.line(
    df,
    x='y',
    y='f(y)',
    title='Plot of f(y) for $dy/dx = y^2 - 4$',
    labels={'y': 'y (Dependent Variable)', 'f(y)': 'Slope (dy/dx)'}
)

# Add a horizontal line at f(y)=0 (equilibrium points)
fig.add_hline(
    y=0,
    line_dash="dash",
    line_color="red",
    annotation_text="Equilibrium Points where f(y) = 0",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

# Customize layout: white background, bigger fonts, centered axes, custom axis label fonts
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title='y',
    yaxis_title='f(y) = dy/dx',
    autosize=False,
    width=600,
    height=600,
    margin=dict(t=50, b=50, l=50, r=50),
    font=dict(size=18),  # default font for ticks/title
    xaxis_title_font=dict(size=20, family='Times New Roman', color='black'),
    yaxis_title_font=dict(size=20, family='Times New Roman', color='black'),
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    paper_bgcolor="white",
    xaxis=dict(
        zeroline=True,
        zerolinewidth=2,
        zerolinecolor='black',
        linecolor='black',
        mirror=True
    ),
    yaxis=dict(
        zeroline=True,
        zerolinewidth=2,
        zerolinecolor='black',
        linecolor='black',
        mirror=True
    )
)

# Show the plot
fig.show()


```


## Style 2

::::{.columns}
:::{.column}

We can also use a two column format for figures that can be smaller. 

We can have some explanatory text here on the left. 

:::
:::{.column}

```{python}
#| echo: false

import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Define the function f(y) from the autonomous equation dy/dx = f(y)
def f(y):
    return y**2 - 4

# Create a range of y values
y_values = np.linspace(-4, 4, 100)
f_y_values = f(y_values)

# Create a pandas DataFrame for Plotly Express
df = pd.DataFrame({'y': y_values, 'f(y)': f_y_values})

# Create a line plot
fig = px.line(
    df,
    x='y',
    y='f(y)',
    title='Plot of f(y) for $dy/dx = y^2 - 4$',
    labels={'y': 'y (Dependent Variable)', 'f(y)': 'Slope (dy/dx)'}
)

# Add a horizontal line at f(y)=0 (equilibrium points)
fig.add_hline(
    y=0,
    line_dash="dash",
    line_color="red",
    annotation_text="",
    annotation_position="bottom right"
)

# Customize layout: white background, bigger fonts, centered axes, custom axis label fonts
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title='y',
    yaxis_title='f(y) = dy/dx',
    autosize=False,
    width=300,
    height=300,
    margin=dict(t=50, b=50, l=50, r=50),
    font=dict(size=18),  # default font for ticks/title
    xaxis_title_font=dict(size=20, family='Times New Roman', color='black'),
    yaxis_title_font=dict(size=20, family='Times New Roman', color='black'),
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    paper_bgcolor="white",
    xaxis=dict(
        zeroline=True,
        zerolinewidth=2,
        zerolinecolor='black',
        linecolor='black',
        mirror=True
    ),
    yaxis=dict(
        zeroline=True,
        zerolinewidth=2,
        zerolinecolor='black',
        linecolor='black',
        mirror=True
    )
)

# Show the plot
fig.show()


```
